newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Dec 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Dec 5.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO DAILY -- The British Foreign Office announced that Hong Kong people who had acquired British passports through the British Nationality Scheme would not be entitled to consular protection if they have dual nationality.
-- Some members of the Legislative Council were planning to demand the Government take measures to stop recent speculative residential properties transactions.

-- WEN WEI PO -- China will take eight measures to reform state enterprises, which will be put to the test in 100 major cities. It said 50 enterprises with potential products and markets but lacking capital will be allowed to be listed.
-- China and Nepal signed an agreement of economic and technological cooperation during the visit of Chinese President Jiang Zemin.

-- APPLE DAILY -- An inspection showed that most public facilities in Hong Kong fail to accomodate disabled people. Because of the inconvenience when going out, many disabled people are forced to stay away from the community.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Textile makers said that the United States planned to place another six garment categories on its "watch list" for illegal transhipments.
-- Shenzhen and Shanghai have been chosen as pilot cities for China's first two rural co-operative banks, as the country works to standarise lending by rural credit co-operatives.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- British and Chinese representatives said they did not anticipate a break-through in the latest plenary meeting of the Joint Liaison Group, while China warned Britain not to create any new obstacles.

-- Beijing pledged to curb a rush by provinces to invest in high-profile industries, but economists said defiance from regional authorities would impede attempts by Beijing to restructure the economy.
